correctness.rationale: The specific positive affine defection advantage follows by inserting the two constant-row payoff gaps in the originating model's equations (1)–(5). On the behavioral nullcline x=h(I), positive equilibria correspond bijectively to g(I)=k in (0,1). The logarithmic derivative of g is strictly decreasing, starts at -1+d/(1+exp(c)), and tends to minus infinity. This certifies each root count, including k=g_0 (the root at zero is excluded) and the double root at k=g_m. The critical equation gives w=d(1-I_m)-1 with w exp(w)=exp(c+d-1), and substitution gives g_m=w/d. The endemic Jacobian has negative trace and determinant -beta I g'(I); the disease-free eigenvalues are -1 and beta(g_0-k). At the fold, with b=-beta I_m(1-I_m), right and left null vectors may be taken as (h'(I_m),1) and (b,1); their pairing is nonzero. Projection of the parameter derivative onto the left null vector gives -beta I_m and projection of the second derivative in the right null direction gives beta I_m g''(I_m), both nonzero, confirming the dynamical saddle-node. The strict witness follows from 2<e<4 by comparing g at 0, 1/10 and 1, not from rounded roots. The source's sufficient threshold and condition (16) specialize as reported; failing them does not contradict the source. No disease-free stability classification at equality or global basin statement is needed. The finite frozen numerical checker was inspected, not run; the analytic argument is decisive.

value.rationale: In this commonly used abstract feedback form, the disease-free linear threshold does not determine how many locally stable stationary states the model has. The exact necessary and sufficient frontier distinguishes this ambiguity from simple threshold crossing, gives a degenerate boundary and clarifies the limitations of the originating sufficient results. The complete classification is useful beyond a single simulated or algebraic witness.
